correctness.rationale: For all a,b and missing-class counts the ratio (2) follows from the exact complete split Laplacian determinant. A direct derivative bound proves the strict monotonicity. Exact cofactor, brute-force tree and coefficient checks reproduced the computations (868 assertions). The infinite conclusion rests on the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The motivating random-subtree spanning problem has a meaningful marked variant on an asymmetric dense graph: one wants to know which vertex class is missing, not just total omitted order. The theorem identifies two distinct strictly positive intensities, asymptotic independence, and a nontrivial monotonic probability function, distinguishing the high-degree clique from the lower-degree independent vertices. It is an exact structural classification with a natural asymptotic regime, not merely a known one-parameter table evaluation.
